articles.title: Got keys to your home after years of delay? You may still claim interest for lost time
articles.summary: Got keys to your dream home after years of waiting? You may still be able to claim interest for the delay.
articles.body: Got keys to your dream home after years of waiting? You may still be able to claim interest for the delay. Homebuyers who take possession of a delayed property can still claim interest for the period during which the developer failed to deliver the flat on time.In a recent order, the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court, presided over by Justice Prashant Kumar, dismissed an appeal by Antriksh Developers and Promoters Pvt Ltd in a dispute over its Antriksh Golf View project in Sector 78, Noida.The court upheld the direction to pay interest to homebuyer Shyam Sunder Agrawal, even though he had accepted possession of the flat.Here’s what happened:Agrawal had booked the flat in 2010, with possession contractually due by November 2012. The developer offered possession only in May 2017. The court also noted that the possession offer was made without the occupancy certificate and other necessary documents. The Uttar Pradesh RERA Appellate Tribunal had directed the developer to pay interest on the amount deposited by the buyer from December 2012 to May 2017 at one percentage point above the Marginal Cost of Fund Based Lending Rate, or MCLR.The court also considered the developer's claim regarding the NGT-related "zero period". It held that any exclusion could apply only to the period actually affected by the restriction and could not wipe out a delay that had already occurred before the restriction came into force.Failure in delivering project: What RERA saysSection 18 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 deals with delayed possession. If a buyer wants to withdraw from a project because of the developer's failure to give possession according to the agreement, the law provides for return of the amount paid along with prescribed interest and compensation.If the buyer does not want to withdraw, the law provides for interest for every month of delay until possession is handed over.The Allahabad HC ruling therefore draws an important distinction between accepting possession and giving up a claim for delay interest. Taking the flat does not, by itself, extinguish the statutory claim for the period of delay.For buyers, the key documents include the agreement for sale, contractual possession date, payment records, possession letter and occupancy or completion documents. The exact interest rate and period for which interest is payable can depend on the applicable RERA rules, contractual terms, court orders and facts of the case.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Ukraine strikes Russian oil refinery, passenger train in overnight drone attacks; 2 dead
articles.summary: Two people were killed in separate Ukrainian drone attacks across Russia overnight, Russian officials said, as the strikes damaged an oil refinery,
articles.body: Two people were killed in separate Ukrainian drone attacks across Russia overnight, Russian officials said, as the strikes damaged an oil refinery, industrial sites and a passenger train.Russia's defence ministry said its air defences destroyed 592 Ukrainian drones during the overnight barrage, reported news agency Reuters.One person was killed and another injured in Belgorod after a Ukrainian drone struck a truck, according to local officials. In Perm, Governor Dmitry Makhonin said one person was killed during what he described as a large-scale drone attack. The region is home to a major oil refinery.Oil refinery forced to halt operationsThe Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Russia's southern Rostov region was also damaged in the attacks.Governor Yuri Slyusar said around 50 drones were destroyed over the region and the strike forced the refinery to temporarily suspend operations. He said there were no reports of casualties there.In Ulyanovsk, eight people were injured after another drone attack damaged industrial and civilian infrastructure, Governor Alexei Russkikh said. The region is home to a major electronics plant.Passenger train hit in SamaraA passenger train travelling from Moscow to Tolyatti was also damaged in the overnight attacks.Russia's state railway operator said an electric locomotive and the train's first carriage were damaged by what it described as external interference on a section of railway in the Samara region.The train driver was injured and rail traffic on the affected section was temporarily suspended.In the Voronezh region, Governor Alexander Gusev said air defences destroyed 88 drones over the regional capital and at least six surrounding districts.Four people were injured there, while residential buildings, vehicles and industrial facilities were damaged, Gusev said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pope Leo heads to France amid assisted dying, abuse debates
articles.summary: First papal state visit to country in 18 years comes as church confronts contentious issues.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV is heading to France for the first official papal visit to the country in 18 years.

The four-day visit begins in Paris on Friday, where Leo will meet President Emmanuel Macron at the Elysee Palace before addressing French officials and civil society.

The first American pope will carry a message centred on human dignity as the Catholic Church in France confronts a newly enacted assisted dying law and the lasting fallout from clerical sexual abuse.

After meeting the president, Leo will deliver an address at UNESCO, attend a service at Notre-Dame Cathedral and join a youth vigil at the Stade de France.

Cardinal Jean-Marc Aveline, head of the French bishops’ conference, said “the defence of the dignity of human life” would be at the heart of Leo’s message.

France enacted a law in August establishing a right to assisted dying under specified conditions for adults suffering from serious and incurable illnesses. The measure had faced strong opposition from the Catholic Church, which teaches that human life should be protected from conception until natural death.

However, Martin Dumont, secretary-general of a religion research institute in France, told the AFP news agency that he would be “very surprised” if the pope adopted a confrontational stance on the issue.

Leo is expected to meet seven survivors of clerical sexual abuse in Lourdes on Sunday. A landmark independent inquiry published in 2021 estimated that about 330,000 people had been abused as minors by clergy or other people associated with the French Catholic Church over seven decades.

Retired French Bishop Marc Stenger told the Reuters news agency that the scandals had “wounded the church deeply and damaged its credibility”.

Survivors have continued to press church leaders for greater accountability despite compensation and safeguarding measures introduced in recent years.

Leo’s visit comes as the Catholic Church seeks to make its voice heard in a country with a deeply rooted tradition of secularism and declining church influence over public policy.

But his message will extend beyond France’s domestic debates. The pope is also due to visit a Paris centre supporting migrants, speak on artificial intelligence and conclude his trip in Metz with a meeting focused on Europe’s role in promoting peace and unity.
